transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Velaris ML), Tomás Alvarez (Velaris Platform), Karen Liu (Velaris AI Ops)

Summary: quick weekly pulse on POC bench results — focus on latency vs incumbent baseline, throughput tuning notes, and next steps to validate production SLOs and security/integration asks. Action items captured at end.

Topics:
- 95th/avg latencies vs baseline
- Throughput (tokens/sec) under different concurrency profiles
- Effects of KV cache warm/cold and quantization profile
- Networking: VPC peering, KMS and data residency
- Cost tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated slots
--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining. on our side it's Maya and Daniel. how are you all?
[00:06] Priya: hey thanks, doing okay. excited to see the numbers. we had a smaller internal smoke test earlier but yeah want to compare to what's live with the incumbent.
[00:12] Tomás: hi all, platform stuff — I'll be watching the networking and throughput details.
[00:15] Karen: hi, I'll focus on security and ops questions.
[00:18] Maya: cool. quick agenda — Daniel will walk results, then we'll talk tradeoffs and next steps. sound good?
[00:22] Daniel: yep. jumping in — we ran three main series over the last week: low-latency traffic (1–4 concurrent requests), medium concurrency (10–20), and high concurrency stress (50–100). each used Velaris prompt set v1 (Priya shared).
[00:38] Daniel: baseline numbers first — incumbent provider reported 95th pctl latency at ~180ms for short prompts (under 256 tokens) at low concurrency, and throughput around 1,800 tokens/sec in their cluster for the same workload. your baseline CSV was the one labelled "incumbent_baseline_0907.csv", right Priya?
[00:55] Priya: yes that's the one. note they have a reserved cluster and some routing caching that we may not be able to replicate one-to-one.
[01:02] Daniel: right. our hosted run on Redwood (default quant profile q4_8 approximate) shows avg latency ~95ms and 95th ~140ms on the short prompt tasks at 1–4 concurrency, with tokens/sec at ~3,200 in that config. important note: 95th improved with prefix/KV cache warm. cold starts added ~30–40ms.
[01:23] Tomás: can you clarify cold vs warm — is that kv cache or model cold load?
[01:27] Daniel: mostly KV cache effects — model binary already resident. with KV warm we keep past context in-memory so next calls are faster. when cache is cold you hit about 170–180ms 95th for same short prompt, so it lines up with incumbent there.
[01:40] Karen: that's promising. what's the variance on medium prompts, say 800 tokens?
[01:44] Daniel: for 800-token generative flows, avg latency per request goes up to ~420ms and 95th ~610ms at low concurrency. throughput measured as tokens/sec per instance dropped to ~1,100. incumbent reported ~1,000 tokens/sec there. quantization profile matters — q8 gives better perf but slight quality diffs on hallucination-sensitive prompts.
[02:06] Priya: how did you run quant tests? any automatic evals?
[02:09] Daniel: we ran n=50 samples across prompts and compared logprobs and a simple QA accuracy harness. delta in accuracy was within 1.5 percentage points between q4_8 and q8 on your eval set, but hallucination cases spiked in certain instruction templates — we flagged those prompts in the csv.
[02:27] Maya: quick commercial note — those perf deltas also map to cost differences. q8 higher throughput means fewer compute seconds but licensing/slot cost may be different on dedicated. we'll send a short model/profile cost matrix.
[02:39] Tomás: networking — we saw a handful of tail latencies attributed to cross-region hops in your hosted test. did you pin region to us-east-1?
[02:46] Daniel: yes, most runs were us-east-1. one run accidentally routed via our fallback edge in us-west-2 — that caused ~40ms extra tail. we'll re-run the medium-concurrency set with strict routing to avoid cross-region fallthrough.
[02:58] Priya: any ops implications if we move to Dedicated? we need predictable throughput and isolation.
[03:03] Maya: Dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools and more predictable throughput; you can configure autoscaling policies and reserve burst. tradeoff is commit cost. for the numbers you want (sustained 3k tokens/sec for short prompts), we can estimate slot counts and give an annual vs monthly commit — I'll share that.
[03:18] Karen: security checklist — do you have SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, KMS integration, audit logs? and can you support VPC peering?
[03:25] Maya: yes — SOC2 Type II in our security pack; SAML and SCIM for provisioning; KMS integrations for Private installs and dedicated slots; audit logs retained for configurable retention. VPC peering supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we do VPC peering via customer-managed connectors. will send docs.
[03:40] Tomás: great. on the benchmark — you mentioned cold KV warm differences, can you show the CSV snippets?
[03:45] Daniel: I pasted excerpts in the shared drive; but to summarize: short prompt, KV warm: p50=88ms p95=140ms p99=210ms; KV cold: p50=120ms p95=170ms p99=290ms. throughput warm ~3.2k t/s, cold ~2.1k t/s.
[04:05] Priya: the p99 matters for us because of user-facing latency spikes — can you do a tail optimization run? maybe batch sizing or micro batching?
[04:12] Daniel: yes. we tried continuous batching vs fixed batching. continuous batching keeps latency SLO better because it dynamically builds batches but requires more complex scheduling. micro-batching (batch size 4–8) lowered p99 by ~10% in our lab but increased avg cost by ~6%. we can tune to your target.
[04:30] Maya: also routing playbook — you can route high-priority traffic to lower-latency pool and background batch to cheaper quantized variant. that preserves user experience while saving $ on cheap workloads.
[04:42] Tomás: how does fallback work if a dedicated slot is full? do requests spill to hosted?
[04:46] Daniel: we have smart routing policies — yes, you can set auto-fallback to hosted API or to a compatible model variant. fallback is configurable by percent and latency threshold.
[04:56] Priya: any perf difference when falling back to the hosted variant?
[04:59] Daniel: small differences — fallback to slightly older checkpoint or different quant profile adds ~20–50ms depending on model/sequence length. we'll show the exact matrix.
[05:07] Karen: data residency — proof that customer data isn't used for model training?
[05:11] Maya: for Dedicated/Private, data stays in your VPC/tenant; we do not use logs for training. for hosted, by default we provide an opt-out and strict controls; our security pack has the language for contracts.
[05:23] (brief side noise)
[05:28] Daniel: okay, moving on to throughput stress tests — we pushed 400 concurrent short requests across 8 instances. our measured aggregate throughput peaked ~25k tokens/sec with 95th client-side latency ~320ms. incumbent reported ~18k t/s under similar cluster size. caveat: their cluster had different hardware and burst policies.
[05:52] Tomás: 25k sounds good — do you have per-instance breakdown?
[05:55] Daniel: yes — per instance tokens/sec was between 2.9–3.4k; variance came from minor queueing and occasional GC on orchestration side. we'll surface the per-instance logs.
[06:06] Priya: interesting. can you reproduce with LRU cache eviction and long-context flows? our real workload has mixed short+long sequences and frequent context shifting.
[06:15] Daniel: we did one mixed-run: 60% short, 40% long. overall throughput dropped ~18% and p95 increased ~12% relative to short-only. LRU eviction and KV cache pressure were the leading causes — suggested mitigations: increase cache size, tune eviction thresholds, or route long-context flows to dedicated slot with more KV memory.
[06:35] Maya: one thing to highlight — quantization + dedicated hardware mapping produced the most consistent throughput; the combo reduced variance.
[06:42] Karen: is there an audit trail for requests? we need per-token billing that's auditable for finance.
[06:48] Maya: yes, token-level usage logs with routing tags and model version are in Console. exportable CSVs and synthetic billing reconciliation reports.
[06:58] (pause, rustling)
[07:03] Priya: on quality — you mentioned q8 had small accuracy delta. can you attach the QA harness results in the next deck? we need examples where hallucination regressed.
[07:12] Daniel: yes, we'll attach the harness output and flagged prompts. quick note: one instruction template that dereferences external IDs caused hallucination under q8 — appears in flagged_prompts_0909.csv.
[07:24] Tomás: about the region routing issue — are you able to guarantee us-east-1 for all production traffic? we have compliance rules.
[07:30] Maya: yes, for Dedicated and Private you can pin region. for Hosted we support regional endpoints and strict routing; for extra guarantee we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[07:40] Karen: on KMS — what's the key rotation cadence and who controls keys?
[07:44] Daniel: you control the keys in customer-managed KMS for Private. rotation policies are customer-managed; for hosted we offer a managed KMS integration but can enable BYOK for enterprises.
[07:56] Priya: what's the expected uplift if we enable aggressive batching and sacrifice a little latency for cost?
[08:01] Daniel: looking at our tests, if you allow 20–30ms extra average latency we can improve tokens/sec by ~25% with batch size tuning; p99 will still be within your target if you route high-priority traffic separately.
[08:14] Maya: should we walk through the CSV summary now or do you want to save time?
[08:18] Priya: let's hit the highlights and follow up on deep dives.
[08:22] Daniel: highlight table: short prompts KV warm: p95 140ms, throughput 3.2k t/s. short prompts cold: p95 170ms, throughput 2.1k. medium (800 tokens): p95 610ms, t/s ~1.1k. stress 400 concurrent: aggregate 25k t/s. q8 yields ~10–15% throughput gain but marginal QA regressions on ~2% of prompts.
[08:45] Maya: important product note — we can provide a canary rollout with traffic split and automatic fallback rules so you can verify in prod without full cutover.
[08:53] Tomás: that would be useful. what's involved from our infra side for a canary?
[08:57] Daniel: just a routing config and a service account; for host-to-host we can manage certificates and VPC connectors. we'll share a runbook.
[09:06] Karen: cost question — if we need sustained 3k t/s and 95th under 160ms, what rough commit would you recommend?
[09:14] Maya: prelim estimate — 3 dedicated slots or equivalent reserved capacity depending on model family and seq-length distribution. I'll put dollar ranges in the pricing sheet and include burst allowances.
[09:26] Priya: any public benchmarks or references we can share internally? we need a couple of short case studies.
[09:31] Maya: yes — we have a performance one-pager and two reference pilots in biotech we'll include.
[09:37] (short pause)
[09:40] Daniel: quick note on tooling — trace hooks and per-route dashboards are available; we instrument token-level latency and can correlate model-version diffs. that helped us find the misrouted us-west run earlier.
[09:53] Priya: perfect. regarding the pilot phase 2, if we do a dedicated slot, how long to provision?
[09:58] Daniel: usually 3–5 business days for Dedicated reservation in the same region; for Private it's longer due to network provisioning. we can accelerate in emergencies.
[10:08] Maya: OK I want to make sure we have concrete next steps. Priya — can you confirm the canonical prompt set and your 95th SLO by Friday 2027-09-18?
[10:16] Priya: yes we can do that.
[10:19] Maya: Daniel — run the extended throughput (50% concurrency 10k tokens) and include KV warm/cold breakdown, per-instance logs, and q4_8 vs q8 comparisons; due 2027-09-21.
[10:27] Daniel: got it.
[10:29] Maya: I'll send the security pack and pricing delta by Thursday 2027-09-16 and propose times for the on-site/remote benchmark week of 09-27.
[10:38] Karen: sounds good — and we'll confirm our internal stakeholders for compliance review.
[10:42] Maya: any other blockers?
[10:44] Tomás: might want a runbook for fallback routing — please include.
[10:48] Daniel: will add to the runbook.
[10:51] Priya: thanks everyone. good session.
[10:53] Maya: great. recap — we'll share logs, security pack, pricing, and proposed schedule. meet again next week same time unless needed earlier.
[10:59] (meeting ends)

Links/Artifacts referenced: shared/velaris/poc/csvs (flagged_prompts_0909.csv, incumbent_baseline_0907.csv, per_instance_logs_0914.zip), security_pack_v2.pdf, pricing_matrix_dedicated.csv

Recorded action items (plain text):
- Daniel: extended throughput test with KV warm/cold; 10k-token run; attach logs (due 2027-09-21)
- Priya: confirm canonical prompt set and 95th SLO target (due 2027-09-18)
- Maya: send security pack (SOC2, KMS notes), pricing delta, and propose on-site times (due 2027-09-16)
